Image2 is the original Buddha line STYLE MASTER only. Image3 is the actual photo of this same Dacheng Hall for geometry verification. Keep elegant fine black lines on purewhite, no shading. Also simplify repetitive tile-direction lines: erase about70percent of the parallel lines inside both large roof planes, retaining only spaced directional hints; leave outline, ridges and eaves unchanged. All other geometry and ornament should stay the same. No people, no labels or text, no watermark. Full canvas1536x1024.

site_recommendation.coordinate_note: Commons实景照片拍摄位置35°35′45.04″N116°59′05.51″E，位于大成殿前露台，作为条目的近似定位；不声称建筑中心或测绘坐标。
site_recommendation.lede: 大成殿居于曲阜孔庙中轴，两重歇山檐下立着盘龙石柱。殿前的露台与阶道，把祭孔仪式的行进和空间秩序连在一起。
facts: 现存大成殿在雍正二年（1724）火灾后重建，雍正八年（1730）竣工。
大殿面阔九间、进深五间，采用重檐歇山顶，黄琉璃瓦覆顶。
前檐十根石柱深雕盘龙，殿前石台阶与露台构成祭孔空间。

initial_prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: a single fine-line architectural illustration for the Chinese heritage collection 访古.
Image 1 is the STYLE MASTER, an existing Vairocana Buddha contour drawing. Match its elegant, delicate, slightly organic thin lines, restrained detail, generous blank areas, and consistent visual density. Image 2 (and subsequent photos if applicable) is SUBJECT GEOMETRY ONLY: draw the actual named monument in that reference, preserving its identifying silhouette, roof type, visible storey count, bay count, openings, and proportions.
Create a refined, sparse BLACK INK ON PURE WHITE line drawing. Use confident fine contours with a few finer internal structural lines. All surfaces remain WHITE; use outlines for doors and windows rather than dark fills. No solid shadows, no broad grey shading, no crosshatching, no pencil grain, no texture, no gradient. No color, no gold, no black background. The white will become transparent and the ink the relevant dynasty color in the website.
Show the complete monument, centered, approximately straight-on at facade level, with verticals vertical and minimal perspective. Use only a few short ground lines. Remove tourists, foliage, vehicles, wires, modern signage, fences obstructing the structure, neighboring distractions and sky. Preserve architectural ornament selectively, without filling every roof tile or brick. No invented features. No labels, letters, calligraphy, dimension lines, captions, watermark, frame or border.
Wide compositions: landscape 1536×1024, entire building occupies about 82% of canvas width, roof/apex and base uncut, balanced breathing room. Tall pagodas: portrait 1024×1536, entire pagoda occupies about 82% of height, centred with equal side margins, apex and base uncut.


Subject: ONLY Dacheng Hall of the Temple of Confucius at Qufu, Shandong (曲阜孔庙大成殿), rebuilt in1730. Image1 is STYLE ONLY. Images2,3,4 show the SAME actual hall, with cropped edges to be extended only to the authentic matching symmetrical roof ends. Preserve a NINE-BAY facade with EXACTLY TEN visible stone dragon columns in a single front row, and two roof tiers: a double-eaved HIP-AND-GABLE roof (重檐歇山顶). This is NOT the nine-bay hipped-roof hall at Dai Temple. Draw the broad upper roof with long ridge, two massive ridge-end ornaments and small corner ridge ornaments, and a second lower surrounding eave, both with gracefully lifted outer corners. No center finial, no third roof tier, no balcony. Keep the long shallow front porch, plain rear wall containing red-in-photo framed geometric lattice doors, and ten stone columns with selectively outlined coiling dragons, easily recognizable as carved stone columns, without filling tiny scales. The lower roof is wider than upper roof. Keep a wide stepped stone terrace with a central broad stairway split by a flat carved stone dragon ramp. Retain historic low stone balustrades as sparse outlines on both sides of central stairs and across the terrace; remove only modern black metal guardrails. The overall silhouette is broad and low, around2to1 width-to-height including roofs and terrace; not a tall pagoda. Remove foreground trees, people, umbrella stalls, incense burner in front of the middle door, signs, signage, flags, lights and all surrounding temple buildings. Keep only empty silhouettes of the central vertical plaque between eaves and small horizontal plaque above the central doorway; absolutely no writing or calligraphy. Reduce elaborate bracket bands and lattice doors to representative fine lines; surfaces all WHITE without black shadow fills. Roof planes are large white fields with ONLY a few separated roof-direction contour strokes; no every-tile repetition and no dense hatch. Full complete exterior from ridge to terrace base, approximately straight-on facade level, centered and vertical, at least8percent whitespace left/right and balanced margin above/below, landscape1536x1024.
